To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

1) we developed a pipeline to automatically extract interpretable features of clinical factors from raw EEG data using deep unsupervised representation learning, 2) these features can be used to accurately predict clinical factors from raw data and to extract interpretable features that are associated with clinical factors, and 3) these features are interpretable in a way that allows for post-hoc analysis by human experts.
we propose a novel pipeline to extract interpretable and denoised EEG features from raw EEG data that can be used in clinical settings to improve the classification accuracy of clinical diagnoses.
we have developed a novel method for extracting interpretable and clinically useful features from EEG that can improve the accuracy of clinical diagnoses.
In summary, our research is concerned with

the development of methods that are able to extract interpretable features from noisy, real world EEG data in a scalable manner that can be used by both clinicians and data scientists to improve clinical outcomes.
the problem of how to best leverage the rich and complex information in the EEG signal to support improved clinical decision making and patient care.
the development of an EEG-based pipeline that can automatically learn and extract interpretable representations of clinical markers from EEG data.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the method we propose can be a useful tool for clinicians, as it can help them in the diagnosis and treatment of mental health disorders.
the method proposed here is a novel and effective approach that allows for the automated detection of interpretable EEG markers of mental health disorders.
we have developed a method for extracting interpretable, clinically-relevant features from EEG data, and that our method is more accurate than a canonical hand-engineered approach.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we are able to extract meaningful and interpretable features of clinical interest from EEG data, and use these features to accurately predict clinical factors, while also denoising the signal.

we have demonstrated a novel method for learning a representation that 1) is more accurate at predicting clinical labels than the canonical hand-engineering method, 2) is interpretable, 3) allows for the extraction of ERPs from single EEG trajectories, 4) is able to automatically extract interpretable clinical markers from the EEG, and 5) can be re-mapped to new clinical labels.
we are able to learn a representation that can 1) automatically detect and denoise ERPs, 2) support fast re-mapping to clinical factors, and 3) be interpreted by clinicians.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of deep learning methods can be leveraged for both improved classification accuracy and human interpretability of clinical EEG data.
unsupervised representation learning can improve interpretability and classification performance of neural markers in the context of clinical EEG data.

unsupervised deep representation learning methods can be used to extract interpretable, clinically relevant features from raw EEG signals, and that these methods can be used as a general framework to address a number of clinical problems in mental health, including the development of objective diagnostic tools and the prediction of clinical course.
